title: Extend Neumann directive parser to capture traction vector and surface set
objective: Parse `% mechanics boundary load --type neumann --traction "x y z" [--surface tag]` directives into the extended BoundaryCondition IR slot.

plan_assets.asset_description: Directive example: % mechanics boundary load --type neumann --traction "0 0 -1000"

scope: Parse --surface <tag> (default to plan-defined fallback if omitted)
Surface symbolic emission and IR construction using P1-1 fields
implementation_steps: Add traction-vector parser (whitespace-split, float convert, length-3 check)
Construct BoundaryCondition with new traction + surface_tag fields
Add unit tests covering parse success and malformed-traction failure
deliverables: Updated frontend/directives.py with Neumann traction + surface parsing
Error message pointing to plan/IR contract on malformed input
acceptance_criteria: % mechanics boundary load --type neumann --traction "0 0 -1000" --surface top → BoundaryCondition(traction=[0,0,-1000], surface_tag='top')
Malformed traction string raises with directive line number

cases: Parse Neumann directive with traction + surface
Parse Neumann directive missing traction → error
Parse Neumann directive with malformed traction string → error

risks: Existing directive grammar may not support multi-token quoted args — mitigation: use shlex or argparse for tokenization

commands.command: uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/ -m 'not slow and not gpu' -q

completion_notes: _mech_boundary now branches on --traction (numeric vs symbolic) and --surface (mapped to surface_tag)
Numeric form requires exactly 3 floats; both arity and non-numeric tokens raise ParseError citing the directive line
Symbolic single-token traction (e.g. 't_bar') still flows through unchanged
